CvText

class CvText[source]

Bases: object

Unicode text and window titles for OpenCV (HighGUI) windows.

Notes

The window name is the key that every HighGUI call uses (imshow, destroyWindow, setMouseCallback…). It is kept ASCII by window_name so that it is the same in every platform; the text the user sees is set apart with set_window_title.

Examples

>>> CvText.window_name("Pantalla de monitorización")
'Pantalla de monitorizacion'

Methods

draw_lines

Draw lines of Unicode text on a BGR frame, wrapping to fit.

font

Return a TrueType font of size pixels (cached).

set_window_title

Show title (Unicode) in the window called name.

window_name

Return an ASCII-only window name derived from title.

wrap

Split text into lines no wider than max_width pixels.

Return an ASCII-only window name derived from title.

Parameters:
titlestr

Translated window title, possibly with accents.

Returns:
str

title without diacritics and non-ASCII characters.

static set_window_title(name, title)[source]

Show title (Unicode) in the window called name.

Parameters:
namestr

Window name given to cv2.namedWindow (see window_name).

titlestr

Text to show in the title bar.

Notes

On Windows the title is set with SetWindowTextW, because cv2.setWindowTitle uses the ANSI API there. If the window is not found, the ASCII name stays as the title. On other platforms cv2.setWindowTitle already handles UTF-8.

Returns:

static wrap(text, font, max_width)[source]

Split text into lines no wider than max_width pixels.

Parameters:
textstr

Text to split; existing line breaks are kept.

fontPIL.ImageFont.ImageFont

Font used to measure the text.

max_widthint

Maximum line width in pixels.

Returns:
list[str]

Lines of text. A single word wider than max_width is kept on its own line.

Examples

>>> from types import SimpleNamespace
>>> font = SimpleNamespace(getlength=len)  # 1 px per character
>>> CvText.wrap("aa bb cc", font, 5)
['aa bb', 'cc']
static draw_lines(img, lines, origin=(20, 20), font_size=20, color=(0, 255, 255), outline_color=(0, 0, 0), outline_width=2, line_spacing=8, margin=20)[source]

Draw lines of Unicode text on a BGR frame, wrapping to fit.

Parameters:
imgnumpy.ndarray

BGR frame (H x W x 3, uint8). It is not modified.

linesIterable[str]

Lines to draw, top to bottom.

origintuple[int, int], optional

Top-left corner (x, y) of the first line, in pixels. Default is (20, 20).

font_sizeint, optional

Font size in pixels. Default is 20.

colortuple[int, int, int], optional

Text color in BGR. Default is (0, 255, 255) (yellow).

outline_colortuple[int, int, int], optional

Outline color in BGR, drawn around each letter for contrast. Default is (0, 0, 0).

outline_widthint, optional

Outline width in pixels; 0 draws no outline. Default is 2.

line_spacingint, optional

Extra space between lines, in pixels. Default is 8.

marginint, optional

Right margin kept free when wrapping, in pixels. Default is 20.

Returns:
numpy.ndarray

New BGR frame with the text drawn.

Notes

Lines are wrapped to the frame width minus origin[0] and margin, but never to less than font_size pixels. Each line advances font_size + line_spacing pixels.
